extracted.intended_audience: designated school officials (DSOs), immigration petitioners and attorneys, employers/agents, and nonimmigrant applicants (M-1, O-1/O-2)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements for M-1 student transfers, practical training, reinstatement, M-2 dependent rules, SEVIS obligations, and O-1/O-2 petition filing and evidentiary criteria. Intended to guide adjudicators, schools, petitioners, and applicants on eligibility, required documentation, and procedural steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: School transfer — Eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student may not transfer to another school after six months from the date the student was first admitted as, or changes nonimmigrant classification to that of, an M-1 student unless unable to remain at the initial school due to circumstances beyond the student's control. A transferring student must: (A) be a bona fide nonimmigrant; (B) have been pursuing a full course of study at the school last authorized; (C) intend to pursue a full course of study at the transfer-in school; and (D) be financially able to attend the transfer-in school.

rubrics_metrics.name: School transfer — Transfer procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must apply to USCIS on Form I-539 or successor form for permission to transfer between schools. Upon application, the student may affect the transfer subject to approval. If approved, the transfer approval date is the program start date on the Form I-20; extension of stay is granted for time necessary to complete the new course of study plus 30 days, or for a total period of one year, whichever is less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Student must notify current school (transfer-out) and identify transfer-in school; transfer-out school must update SEVIS to show transfer-out, indicate transfer-in school, and input release date; transfer-in school may generate Form I-20 but cannot access SEVIS record until release date; Form I-539 must be submitted upon receipt of transfer-in Form I-20; student may enroll at next available term and must notify DSO immediately upon beginning attendance; transfer-in school must update SEVIS registration per §214.3(g)(2)(iii); if transfer application denied or student transfers without complying, student is out of status and SEVIS record must be terminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Student not pursuing full course — Reinstatement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If an M-1 student who has not been pursuing a full course of study desires to attend a different school, the student must apply for reinstatement to student status under paragraph (m)(16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in educational objective — prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student may not change educational objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment — general prohibition for M-1 students
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided in paragraph (m)(14) (practical training), an M-1 student may not accept employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — Authorization conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporary employment for practical training may be authorized only after completion of the student's course of study. The proposed employment must (A) be recommended for the purpose of practical training; (B) be related to the student's course of study; and (C) be, to the DSO's information and belief, employment not reasonably available in the student's country of foreign residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — Application process and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student must apply for permission to accept employment for practical training on Form I-765 with the applicable fee, accompanied by a properly endorsed Form I-20 by the DSO. The application must be submitted before the program end date but not more than 90 days before the program end date. The DSO must certify on Form I-538 the required conditions (see authorization conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DSO endorsement and Form I-538 certification must state that the employment is recommended for practical training, related to the course of study, and not reasonably available in the student's foreign residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — Duration and EAD requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: When authorized, the M-1 student will be issued an Employment Authorization Document (EAD) and may not begin employment until the EAD is issued. One month of employment authorization is granted for each four months of full-time study completed. Aggregate practical training may not exceed six months. Employment authorization will not be granted if the student cannot complete the requested training within six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — Temporary absence and readmission
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 student granted practical training who temporarily departs the United States may be readmitted for the remainder of the authorized period shown on Form I-20, but must be returning to perform the authorized practical training. A student may not be readmitted to begin practical training that was not authorized prior to departure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — Effect of strike or labor dispute
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorization for employment for practical training is automatically suspended upon certification by the Secretary of Labor (or designee) to DHS that a strike or labor dispute involving a work stoppage of workers is in progress in the occupation at the place of employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ‘Place of employment’ means wherever the employer or joint employer does business.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical training — SEVIS process
rubrics_metrics.description: The DSO must update the student's record in SEVIS to recommend approval for practical training and generate a SEVIS Form I-20 with the recommendation for the student to submit to USCIS with Form I-765.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision on extension/transfer/practical training applications — notification and no appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS will notify the applicant of its decision and, if denied, of the reason(s) for the denial. The applicant may not appeal the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement to student status — Eligibility criteria (general standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: USCIS may consider reinstating a student who requests reinstatement on Form I-539 accompanied by a properly completed Form I-20 indicating the DSO's recommendation only if the student satisfies the listed criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criteria include: (A) not out of status more than 5 months at filing (unless exceptional circumstances caused delay and request filed as promptly as possible); (B) no record of repeated or willful violations of DHS regulations; (C) currently pursuing or intending to pursue a full course of study at the school issuing the Form I-20; (D) has not engaged in unlawful employment; (E) is not deportable on any ground other than section 237(a)(1)(B) or (C)(i) of the Act; and (F) establishes by a detailed showing either (1) the violation resulted from circumstances beyond the student's control (examples: serious injury/illness, closure of institution, natural disaster, inadvertence/oversight/neglect by the DSO) but not instances of repeated violations or willful failure by the student, or (2) the violation relates to a reduction in course load that a DSO could have authorized and failure to approve reinstatement would result in extreme hardship to the student.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement — Decision and SEVIS update
rubrics_metrics.description: The adjudicating officer will update SEVIS to reflect USCIS's decision. If USCIS does not reinstate the student, the student may not appeal the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spouse and children of M-1 student — Forms, employment, and study rules
rubrics_metrics.description: M-2 spouse and minor children will each be issued an individual Form I-20. M-2 spouses and children may not accept employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post-secondary/vocational: M-2 spouse or child may enroll in less than a full course of study at SEVP-certified schools; to engage in a full course of post-secondary study they must change status to F-1, M-1, or J-1 before beginning. Avocational or recreational study up to full-time is allowed. M-2 children may engage in full-time elementary or secondary (K–12) study. Enrolling in unauthorized study violates M-2 status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current name and address — notification and SEVIS update requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A student must inform DHS and the DSO of any legal name change or change of address within 10 days, in a manner prescribed by the school. This satisfies the 8 CFR 265.1 DHS notification requirement by providing notice to the DSO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The DSO must enter address information into SEVIS within 21 days of student notification. Except where the student cannot receive mail at residence, the address must be the actual physical residence, not a mailing address. If a mailing address is provided, the school must maintain and provide upon request the actual physical location where the student resides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student — Applicability and definition
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Border commuter student’ means a national of Canada or Mexico admitted as an M-1 student to enroll in a full course of study, albeit on a part-time basis, in a certified school located within 75 miles of a U.S. land border, who maintains actual residence in their country of nationality and seeks admission at a land border port-of-entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules do not apply to a national of Canada or Mexico who is residing in the U.S. while attending as an M-1, or enrolled in a full course as defined in paragraph (m)(9).

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student — Reduced course load authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: A DSO may authorize an eligible border commuter student to enroll in a course load below that otherwise required for a full course of study, provided the reduced load is consistent with the border commuter student's certified course of study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student — Period of stay limit
rubrics_metrics.description: An M-1 border commuter student is not entitled to the additional 30-day period of stay otherwise available under paragraph (m)(5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Border commuter student — Employment restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: A border commuter student may not be authorized to accept any employment in connection with M-1 status, except for practical training as provided in paragraph (m)(14).

rubrics_metrics.name: Remittance of SEVIS fee for M-1/M-3 applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien applying for M-1 or M-3 nonimmigrant status to enroll in a program at an SEVP-certified vocational institution is required to pay the SEVIS fee to DHS per §214.13, except as otherwise provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Parents and children of section 101(a)(27)(I) special immigrants — N status eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Parent of a child accorded special immigrant status under section 101(a)(27)(I)(i) may, upon application, be granted status under section 101(a)(15)(N)(i) as long as the permanent resident child remains a ‘child’ per section 101(b)(1). Children of parents granted N(i) status, or of parents granted special immigrant status under 101(a)(27)(I)(ii)–(iv), may be granted status under 101(a)(15)(N)(ii) for as long as each remains a child.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission/extension: N nonimmigrant may be admitted for not to exceed three years with extensions in increments up to three years; status terminates when the child no longer qualifies as a child under section 101(b)(1). Employment: N nonimmigrants are authorized employment incident to status without restrictions as to location or type.

rubrics_metrics.name: O classifications — General (O-1, O-2, O-3) and petition prerequisite
rubrics_metrics.description: Under section 101(a)(15)(O), a qualified alien may be authorized to come to the U.S. to perform services related to an event if petitioned for by an employer. O-1 applies to aliens with extraordinary ability in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics or extraordinary achievement in motion picture/television; O-2 applies to accompanying aliens coming solely to assist an O-1; O-3 applies to spouse/child accompanying O-1/O-2. The petitioner must file a petition with the Service for determination of eligibility before the alien may apply for a visa or seek admission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph sets forth the standards and procedures applicable to these classifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of O classifications — who qualifies
rubrics_metrics.description: O-1: individual with extraordinary ability (sciences, arts, education, business, athletics) demonstrated by sustained national or international acclaim, or extraordinary achievement in motion picture/television. O-2: accompanying alien who assists an O-1 and possesses critical skills/experience not of a general nature. O-3: spouse or child accompanying/following-to-join O-1/O-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition filing — General procedural rules for O-1/O-2
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as provided elsewhere, a petitioner seeking O-1 or O-2 classification shall file the prescribed USCIS form. Petition may not be filed more than one year before the actual need. O-1/O-2 petitions are adjudicated at the appropriate Service Center. Only one beneficiary may be included on an O-1 petition; O-2 aliens must be filed on separate petitions. An O-1 or O-2 petition may only be filed by a U.S. employer, a U.S. agent, or a foreign employer through a U.S. agent. A foreign employer may not directly petition for an O alien and must use a U.S. agent. A U.S. agent petitioning on behalf of a foreign employer must be authorized to file and accept service of process on behalf of the foreign employer. An O alien may not self-petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to accompany an O petition
rubrics_metrics.description: Petitions shall be accompanied by: (A) the evidence specified in the particular section for the classification; (B) copies of any written contracts between petitioner and beneficiary or, if none, a summary of terms of the oral agreement; (C) an explanation of the nature of the events/activities, beginning and ending dates, and a copy of any itinerary; and (D) a written advisory opinion(s) from the appropriate consulting entity or entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of documentation for O petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation such as affidavits, contracts, awards must reflect the nature of the alien's achievement and be executed by an officer or responsible person of the institution/organization where the work was performed. Affidavits from present/former employers or recognized experts certifying recognition and ability must specifically describe recognition and ability in factual terms and state the affiant's expertise and how they acquired the information. Legible photocopies may be submitted in lieu of originals, but originals must be submitted if requested by the Director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other filing situations — itineraries, multiple employers, change/amended petitions, multiple beneficiaries, traded athletes
rubrics_metrics.description: A petition requiring work in more than one location must include an itinerary with dates and locations. If beneficiary will work concurrently for more than one employer during the same period, each employer must file a separate petition unless an established agent files. If an O-1 or O-2 in the U.S. seeks to change employers, the new employer must file a petition and request an extension; O-2 may change only with a change by the principal O-1. An amended petition must be filed to reflect material changes in terms/eligibility. More than one O-2 accompanying alien may be included on a petition if assisting the same O-1 for same events/period/location (up to 25 beneficiaries). For traded professional O-1 athletes, employment authorization continues automatically for 30 days after acquisition by a new organization during which new petition should be filed; if filed within 30 days, the athlete is deemed in valid O-1 status until adjudicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agents as petitioners — conditions and obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: A U.S. agent may file petitions for traditionally self-employed workers or where an agent arranges short-term employment with numerous employers, and where a foreign employer uses a U.S. agent. An agent performing as employer must provide the contractual agreement specifying wage and other terms. An agent may file for multiple employers as representative if supporting documentation includes a complete itinerary with dates, names/addresses of actual employers and locations, and a contract between employers and beneficiary. A foreign employer through a U.S. agent remains responsible for complying with employer sanctions provisions of section 274A and 8 CFR part 274a.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The burden is on the agent to explain terms/conditions of employment and provide required documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for O-1 — general evidentiary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Extraordinary ability in sciences, arts, education, business, or athletics, or extraordinary achievement in motion picture/television, must be established for an individual. An O-1 petition must be accompanied by evidence that the work the alien is coming to continue is in the area of extraordinary ability and that the alien meets the specific evidentiary criteria in paragraphs (o)(3)(iii) or (iv).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions relevant to O-1 adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: Key definitions: 'Arts' includes any field of creative activity (fine arts, visual arts, culinary arts, performing arts, and essential persons supporting performances). 'Event' means activities like a scientific project, conference, tour, exhibit, business project, academic year, etc., including related short vacations or promotional appearances; a group of related activities may be an event. 'Extraordinary ability in the arts' means distinction — a high level of achievement evidenced by being prominent, renowned, leading, or well-known. 'Extraordinary ability' in science/education/business/athletics means being in the very top small percentage of the field. 'Extraordinary achievement' in motion picture/television means a very high level of accomplishment evidenced by recognition as outstanding or leading. 'Peer group' means a group/organization comprised of practitioners in the alien's occupation; collective bargaining representatives may be considered appropriate peer groups for consultation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary criteria for O-1 — science, education, business, or athletics
rubrics_metrics.description: An alien must demonstrate sustained national or international acclaim and recognition by providing either (A) receipt of a major internationally recognized award (e.g., Nobel Prize); or (B) at least three of the following: (1) documentation of nationally/internationally recognized prizes or awards; (2) documentation of membership in associations requiring outstanding achievement as judged by national/international experts; (3) published material in professional or major trade publications or major media about the alien's work; (4) evidence of participation as a judge of others' work on a panel or individually; (5) evidence of original scientific, scholarly, or business-related contributions of major significance; (6) evidence of authorship of scholarly articles in the field; (7) evidence of employment in a critical or essential capacity for organizations of distinguished reputation; (8) evidence of commanding or expecting to command a high salary or substantial remuneration. If these criteria do not readily apply, comparable evidence may be submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary criteria for O-1 — arts
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify in the arts, the alien must be recognized as prominent in the field, demonstrated by (A) nomination for or receipt of significant national or international awards (e.g., Academy Award, Emmy, Grammy, Director's Guild Award); or (B) at least three of: (1) evidence of performing/will perform as lead/starring participant in productions/events of distinguished reputation (critical reviews, publicity, contracts, endorsements); (2) evidence of national/international recognition evidenced by critical reviews or published materials; (3) evidence of performing/will perform in lead/critical roles for organizations of distinguished reputation evidenced by articles or testimonials; (4) record of major commercial or critically acclaimed successes evidenced by title, rating, box office receipts, TV ratings, or other occupational achievements; (5) significant recognition for achievements from organizations, critics, government agencies, or recognized experts (testimonials must clearly indicate author's authority); (6) evidence of commanding or expecting to command a high salary or substantial remuneration relative to others in the field. Comparable evidence may be submitted if criteria do not readily apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary criteria for O-1 — motion picture or television industry
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for extraordinary achievement in motion picture/television, the alien must have been nominated for or received significant national/international awards (e.g., Academy Award, Emmy, Grammy, Director's Guild Award); or provide at least three of: (1) evidence of performing/will perform as lead/starring participant in productions/events of distinguished reputation; (2) evidence of national/international recognition evidenced by critical reviews or published materials; (3) evidence of performing/will perform in lead/critical roles for distinguished organizations evidenced by articles or testimonials; (4) record of major commercial or critically acclaimed successes (title, rating, box office, TV ratings); (5) evidence of significant recognition for achievements from organizations/critics/government agencies/recognized experts (testimonials must show author authority); (6) evidence of commanding or expecting to command a high salary or substantial remuneration compared to others in the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for O-2 — general and evidentiary criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: An O-2 accompanying alien provides essential support to an O-1 artist or athlete and may not accompany O-1 aliens in science, business, or education. The O-2 must be petitioned for in conjunction with the O-1. To qualify, the O-2 must be coming to assist in the O-1's performance, be an integral part of the actual performances or events, and possess critical skills and experience with the O-1 that are not of a general nature and not possessed by U.S. workers. For motion picture/television production, the O-2 must have skills/experience with the O-1 that are critical based on a pre-existing longstanding working relationship or because significant production will take place both inside and outside the U.S. and continuing participation is essential to successful completion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence must establish current essentiality, critical skills, and substantial experience performing the critical skills/essential support; for specific productions, evidence must show significant production took/ will take place outside and inside the U.S. and continuing participation is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultation requirement for O petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Consultation with an appropriate U.S. peer group (or persons with expertise), labor and/or management organization regarding the nature of the work and the alien's qualifications is mandatory before approval of an O-1 or O-2 petition, except as provided in limited exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, evidence of consultation must be a written advisory opinion from the appropriate peer group/labor/management organization with expertise in the specific field, submitted with the petition. If the advisory opinion is unfavorable it must set forth specific supporting facts. Advisory opinions must be signed by an authorized official. Written evidence of consultation is to be included in the record of every approved O petition (with exceptions). Consultations are advisory and not binding. Exception: for arts/entertainment/athletics petitions meriting expeditious handling, Service may solicit an advisory opinion and the organization has 24 hours to respond; Service shall adjudicate after receipt of response.
